newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Vanclief says EU likely ok altered canola.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Vanclief says EU likely ok altered canola.

text.p: Canadian Agriculture Minister Lyle Vanclief said on Monday he was confident the European Union would approve genetically-altered canola for human use.

"I'm confident that our regulatory process here is one that can assure end-users that biotechnologically developed products are safe and that's the bottom line," Vanclief told Reuters in an interview.
Canada exported 5.3 percent of its canola seed to EU member nations in calendar 1996, Statistics Canada said. Transgenic Canadian canola seed is approved in Japan, Mexico and the United States.
"It's certainly not something we're going to let up on," Vanclief said.

Two hybrid varieties of genetically-altered Canadian canola seed produced by Plant Genetics Systems have now been approved by the EU commission, two more PGS varieties were pending and one Monsanto Co variety was submitted to France for consideration by the 14 other members, said Ian Thomson, deputy director of Agriculture Canada's Eastern Hemisphere Trade Policy Division.
